text.p: Following are the main stories in Thursday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad reiterated on Tuesday that China does not pose a threat to security in East Asia, inspite of overlapping claims over the Spratly islands. Mahathir's comments came at the Global Panel discussion at The Hague, Netherlands.
- The Rent Control Act, in place for the last 20 years, was repealed by the Malaysian government, allowing owners of buildings built before 1948 to raise rents or to develop their properties.

- Malaysian Mining Corporation said on Tuesday that it had been prepared to take up a 20 percent stake in the Bakun hydroelectric dam project in Sarawak state, but would now focus its resources on the East Coast Highway project.

- Olympia Industries Bhd is to diversify its construction activities. The group will remain focused on residential construction activities, but is actively pursuing work in office, hotel, retail and infrastructure projects.

- Telekom Malaysia Bhd feels that the deadline for the liberalisation of the global telecommunications industry under the World Trade Organisation, should be flexible. Telekom chief executive Mohamed Said Mohamed Ali, said the terms for the liberalisation should take into account differing economic levels.
- Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad will arrive in Medina, Saudia Arabia on Thursday for the first-ever official visit by a Malaysian premiere to the gulf state.

- The state government of Penang Island is studying a site which could hold the proposed 'third link' connecting the island to the mainland. Construction company Mekar Idaman, has been asked to submit detailed proposals for the scheme which would involve the construction of an 11km bridge connected to a tunnel.
- The Malaysian government will decide whether to allow Malaysian Airline System Bhd to raise its international air fares by three percent, in three weeks.
